narrative.overview: pmview is the surface a human watches while autonomous agents work. Its job is to let a supervisor scan the whole state of a change-and-memory workflow and act on the one thing that needs them — so the interface stays calm, legible, and out of the way. Hierarchy is carried by weight, tonal panels, and hairline rules rather than color or ornament. The world is light-and-dark twins that share one set of shape, spacing, and motion tokens and swap only their color primitives. Surfaces are flat at rest and depth is a response to intent: cards and list items lift a single pixel with a soft shadow the moment the operator hovers a target.
keyCharacteristics: Flat at rest, one-pixel lift on hover — depth means 'actionable'.
Accent used sparingly: interactive and selected states only.
Tonal panels + 1px lines do the structural work, in both themes.
One motion grammar: ease-out, 120–180ms, honored down to prefers-reduced-motion.
System sans for reading, mono strictly for identifiers and data.

rules.name: The Accent-Is-A-Verb Rule
rules.body: Signal Blue only appears on something the operator can interact with or has selected. If a blue element does nothing, it's a bug.

rules.name: The Twin-World Rule
rules.body: Light and dark differ only in the nine color primitives; shape, spacing, type, and motion tokens are shared. Never fork a component's geometry per theme.

rules.name: The Mono-Means-Data Rule
rules.body: Monospace is for identifiers, data, and measurements — never as a costume for 'technical'. Prose is always sans.

rules.name: The Flat-Until-Touched Rule
rules.body: A surface is flat at rest. Shadow appears as a response to hover, focus, or the toast — never as static decoration.

rules.name: The Name-First Rule
rules.body: In any id · type · name line, the human-meaningful name is the darkest, largest-weight token; ids and types recede to muted mono.

rules.name: The Persisted-Chrome Rule
rules.body: Drawer width and dock side are user state, not layout defaults — remember them across opens, never reset them on navigation.

rules.name: The One-Hue-Per-Category Rule
rules.body: Map edge types and status onto the existing semantic tokens (accent/ok/warn/danger) and differentiate with drawn icons; never invent a new hue for a category.

dos: Do reach for a spacing, radius, type, or color token for every value; the CSS custom properties on :root are the source of truth and the DESIGN.md frontmatter mirrors them.
Do keep the accent for interactive and selected states only.
Do let hover lift signal actionability — 1px translate + shadow-raised, on ease-out 120–180ms.
Do tint secondary text on any colored surface from that hue or Ink Muted — never a flat gray drop-in.
Do keep light and dark identical except for the nine color primitives.
donts: Don't introduce a build step, framework, CSS-in-JS, or npm dependency — the styling contract is plain CSS + class names shared with app.js.
Don't add a colored border-left/border-right above 1px, gradient text, or zero-blur block shadows.
Don't use monospace as decoration; reserve it for identifiers and data.
Don't rename or drop the component class names — they are the API between style.css and app.js.
Don't ship a hover/focus state without a resting counterpart, or motion without honoring prefers-reduced-motion.
